claims.claim: Public GitHub Pages demo for a reproducible business data-quality case study.
Public v0.2.0 release is available on GitHub.
GHCR container image is published from main and can run the FastAPI service.
Automated test suite passes locally and in GitHub Actions, including the business problem casebook verifier.
Support-ticket case study detects duplicate IDs, missing routing fields, negative amounts, and outliers.
The API exposes a PostgreSQL support-ticket agent endpoint that reuses the read-only adapter and returns a safe disabled fallback when no model key is configured.
Support-ticket case study quantifies 4 issue categories across duplicate ticket IDs, missing routing fields, negative amounts, and amount outliers.
The project publishes a generated outcome summary that maps the support-ticket quality failures to business risk and remediation actions.
The project maps support-ticket quality findings to 4 business risk areas, 3 high-priority actions, and 4 owner handoffs without claiming external adoption.
The project publishes a Docker Compose reviewer path with a seeded PostgreSQL support-ticket table, read-only database user, and 3 local review routes without claiming external reviewer completion.

The project publishes a generated API smoke report that verifies 6 FastAPI routes for health, catalog, profiling, deterministic reports, disabled agent fallback, and incident Markdown export without claiming production uptime.
The project publishes a generated local performance baseline for 2 FastAPI routes and 24 measured endpoint calls without claiming production latency or hosted traffic.
The project publishes a generated demo usage baseline that verifies public demo entrypoints and tracks feedback issues, GitHub stars, and forks without claiming visitor analytics or product adoption.

The project publishes a generated business-data intake baseline covering bounded CSV uploads, read-only PostgreSQL context, 4 integration endpoints, 3 upload limits, and 6 API tests without claiming production datasets.

The project publishes a generated community growth baseline covering 4 issue templates, 5 configured labels, contribution guidance, public feedback entrypoints, and current public counts without claiming community adoption.
The project publishes a generated impact review packet that maps a support-operations data-quality case study to verified business-risk metrics, evidence links, and not-claimed adoption limits.

The project publishes a generated casebook that explains a support-operations dashboard quality failure mode, detected risks, evidence-backed findings, root-cause hypotheses, and remediation owner handoffs.
The project publishes a generated traction dashboard that maps live project surfaces, review channels, tracked funnel steps, and resume-upgrade thresholds to public evidence.
Reports include deterministic verification for evidence support, field references, sensitive values, unsupported LLM evidence, action coverage, and score bounds.
Sanitized run traces can be persisted with TRACE_DB_PATH and recovered by trace id after process restart.
The API can retrieve recent sanitized traces, recurring checks, and recurring root-cause titles for a dataset.
The project publishes a generated artifact that retrieves 3 recurring incident patterns from sanitized support-ticket traces without claiming external production incidents.
The LLM tool-calling agent can retrieve sanitized dataset memory inside the agent loop so recurring checks and incident patterns from prior runs can inform follow-up planning.
The LLM tool-calling agent can retrieve source-cited business rules after quality checks so remediation guidance can reference business constraints instead of only generic data statistics.

The project publishes a generated observability artifact covering trace ids, report types, fallback status, verification status, dataset memory, and tool-call previews without claiming production monitoring.

The project publishes deterministic model telemetry for a mocked LLM agent run, including model name, prompt version, model call count, token count, estimated cost, latency, timeout, retry budget, and raw-prompt logging status without claiming paid model benchmark results.
The project verifies 7 allowed agent tools, 3 rejected unsafe PostgreSQL queries, sensitive-field redaction, disabled fallback, and 6 report verifier rules without claiming a formal security audit.

The project publishes a generated scorecard summarizing the public demo, release, container image, CI tests, verified resume claims, agent capabilities, reviewer paths, and honest zero-adoption baselines.

The project publishes generated recruiter-facing resume bullets, a LinkedIn project description, a 30-second pitch, interview talking points, evidence links, and honest adoption baselines without claiming unverified adoption or production usage.

The project publishes a recruiter-ready evidence pack with application links, verified outcome numbers, resume bullets, an email attachment note, an interview opening, review order, and honest adoption baselines.
The project publishes outreach messages, review paths, tracking rules, and target feedback metrics to collect real public feedback without inflating current adoption.
The project publishes a three-week pilot plan with participant segments, feedback evidence rules, success thresholds, issue labels, and resume upgrade rules before adoption claims are allowed.
Reports rank root-cause hypotheses by confidence and attach supporting checks, tool evidence, and recommended actions.

The project publishes a generated evaluation summary covering status accuracy, finding recall, evidence support, fallback behavior, report-tool usage, report attachment, and latency across 3 scenarios.

The project publishes an eval artifact that verifies the LLM agent exposes 7 allowed tools and recommends relevant quality checks across 3 dataset scenarios without claiming paid model benchmark results.
The project publishes a generated feedback artifact with accepted/needs-review labels for 3 root-cause hypotheses without claiming external product feedback.
The project publishes a generated OpenAPI contract covering 6 core integration endpoints for business data, agent reports, trace lookup, dataset memory, and incident export.
Public metrics are tracked without inflating stars, forks, watchers, issues, release, container, or test count.
Resume-ready claims are summarized in a public Markdown page with current metrics and not-claimed signals.
The project has a public feedback issue template and a feedback log that starts from an honest zero-feedback baseline.
Feedback and reproducible reports are tracked through a public metrics artifact generated from issue labels.
Stars, forks, watchers, issues, release, commit, and test count are tracked as an append-only JSONL history.
The project publishes a resume-safe public metrics summary that combines adoption, feedback, CI, release, outcome, and agent-readiness signals while preserving zero-user and zero-feedback baselines.
A scheduled GitHub Actions workflow verifies the public demo, release page, business-impact artifact, outcome evidence manifest, and adoption metrics remain reachable.
The project documents implemented LLM agent capabilities separately from partial embedding-backed RAG, observability, evaluation, and feedback-informed memory work.

not_claimed.reason: No external feedback issue has been submitted yet.
The project demonstrates a realistic business workflow, not verified enterprise production adoption.
